item.title: Trump ‘pulls the rug’ on Ukraine, nine days of diesel, Houthis hit Saudi – with Larry Johnson
item.description: Olga and Tara welcome Larry Johnson, former CIA officer, to break down the US-Russia diesel deal and what it means for Ukraine, the tension between the CIA and Trump, the roots of the Houthi-Saudi conflict, and how political fragmentation in the US and Europe could shape what comes next. Is the US-Russia diesel deal as significant as it sounds? Johnson argues it is a very good deal for Russia – and a meaningless one for the US. Why does he point to a first shipment of 2.7 million barrels – against 3.5 million barrels of daily US consumption? Did the deal violate laws Trump himself signed? And can it hold if, as Johnson claims, the CIA is a “wild card” pursuing its own agenda? Can Washington really pressure Kiev? What would a halt to satellite data or a Starlink shutdown change on the battlefield? Why does Johnson say Russia refuses a ceasefire, and what does he believe changed in Russia’s approach after the Starobelsk college attack? What does Johnson mean when he calls Europe the “canary in the mineshaft” ? Could Riyadh use its Treasury holdings to pull the US into its conflict with the Houthis? And with Trump caught in the Iran conflict before the midterms, does Johnson’s reading of US politics hold up?

item.title: Europe’s sleepwalking leaders, mercurial Trump, pragmatic US, UN Reform — with Dmitry Polyanskiy
item.description: Olga Bataman and Tara Reade welcome Ambassador Dmitry Polyanskiy, Russia’s Permanent Representative to the OSCE, for the Russian perspective on the risk of a direct conflict with Europe, America’s role in the peace talks, and the future of the United Nations. Is Europe sleepwalking into a direct conflict with Russia? Why does Ambassador Polyanskiy say Europe has inched closer to one, and that a single incident could be enough to trigger it? And why does he argue that unpopular European leaders stay in power while leading their populations toward confrontation? Is Washington a mediator or a source of pressure? Why does Ambassador Polyanskiy call Trump “mercurial” while describing US interests as “pragmatic” ? How does he read the mixed signals — peace talks, a sanctions bill headed for Trump’s signature and a planned US base in Poland — and why does he say Russia is not counting on America’s help? And why does he say Europe and Zelensky are trying to derail the understandings reached in Anchorage? Is there a way back? Why does he say Russia’s door to diplomacy remains open, and that the first step is a clear declaration that neither side plans to attack the other? What would a European security “equation” built together with Russia look like — and can Europe move away from a zero-sum approach toward peaceful coexistence? And is the UN slowly dying – or, as Ambassador Polyanskiy argues, are Western countries holding Security Council reform “hostage” ?

item.title: Zelensky’s midterm gamble, profiting from the Ukraine war, Starlink leverage – with Garland Nixon
item.description: Olga and Tara welcome political analyst Garland Nixon to discuss the public clash between Trump and Zelensky, how money matters define the future of the Ukraine war, the upcoming midterms in the US, and protests in Kiev and Europe. Is the new spat between Trump and Zelensky a media show, or a battle between competing factions in Washington and Europe over how to deal with Russia? Could Starlink be used as leverage to push Zelensky toward negotiations? Is Zelensky growing bolder because he expects the Democrats to win the midterms? And is Ukraine’s collapse a matter of “when,” not “if” ? Who benefits from prolonging the war in Ukraine? Why do European leaders remain politically trapped in a conflict tied to hundreds of billions of dollars in bonds and investments? And what would happen to Russia’s frozen assets if the conflict ended and Moscow demanded its money back? Can any deal survive with the US being “a group of warring factions” ? And what could Republican divisions, a “lame-duck” Trump, or an impeachment battle mean for Ukraine after the midterms? Are the protests and unrest across Europe driven by immigration, or by austerity and war spending? What does Garland mean by an “illusion of democracy,” and why could more political violence follow?

item.title: Ukraine’s vanishing men, Trump’s Jimmy Carter problem, stalling peace deals – with Ben Swann
item.description: Olga and Tara welcome investigative journalist Ben Swann – creator of the acclaimed Zelensky Unmasked series – for a wide-ranging conversation on the war in Ukraine that is draining a generation, Trump’s risk of becoming another Jimmy Carter, schisms within US intelligence agencies, Russia’s recent elections, and much more. Is Ukraine’s male population being sent to the front against its will, and why has fighting shifted almost entirely to drones? Why does Swann argue that the war is being run less from the Pentagon and more from the CIA – and what does that mean for who actually controls US policy? Why does Swann call the latest Russia sanctions bill “toothless,” and what does he think it reveals about Washington’s real priorities? Is Trump boxed in by agencies and allies he underestimated? What drove Trump’s decision to strike Iran despite warnings from his own Joint Chiefs chairman and Tulsi Gabbard – and why didn’t it go as planned? What do competing factions within the CIA and other intelligence agencies mean for Trump’s ability to change course?

item.title: Putin-Xi-Trump meeting, a third US carrier toward Iran, Crimean Bridge attack – with Matt Weinglass
item.description: Olga and Tara are joined by Matt Weinglass, anchor and founder of the Homeless Left podcast, recorded as the Putin-Xi-Trump meeting in Shenzhen is about to begin. Does a “family photo” of three leaders say more than any signed agreement? Is the world still unipolar, or is the meeting itself evidence that it no longer is? Why do US headlines call it an “ego trip” while the hosts see a chance for diplomacy? Could this meeting become a “Yalta 2.0” – or are corporate technocrats and neocons actively working to derail open-source AI cooperation and diplomatic breakthroughs? After the midterms, can a lame-duck Trump deliver anything Russia can rely on? Does it matter whether he knew about the Crimean Bridge attack, or are decisions made above him? Why send a third US aircraft carrier toward Iran? Are recent “dirty bomb” narratives and sudden nationwide infrastructure outages in the US part of a recycled Iraq-era playbook designed to keep the public in a state of fear? And how can Moscow or Tehran trust any negotiated deal if Washington’s signature can be broken by the next political shift?

item.title: IMF as a tool of the West, two unnecessary wars, killing the dollar – with Paulo Nogueira Batista Jr.
item.description: Olga and Tara welcome Professor Paulo Nogueira Batista Jr., former Executive Director for Brazil at the IMF (2007–2015) and a founding member of the BRICS New Development Bank. Is the dollar losing ground because of BRICS – or is the United States undermining its own currency through sanctions? How did the decision to freeze Russian assets change the way countries like China view the dollar? And what does this mean for the future of global finance? What did the Putin-Xi-Trump trilateral meeting reveal about the balance of power between the three countries? Can their Joint Declaration Toward Peace lead to concrete results, or are the geopolitical divisions too deep? And what are the prospects for ending the war in Ukraine? How did the US intervention in Venezuela embolden Washington to attack Iran, and what does this mean for the geopolitical landscape in Latin America? Could Cuba become Washington’s next target? What did Brazil’s October 2026 election mean for the country’s sovereignty? And can BRICS and a more multipolar world offer countries greater protection from Western political and economic pressure?

item.title: Trump’s changed, Iran and Ukraine as forever wars, midterms don’t matter – with Jimmy Dore
item.description: Olga Bataman and Tara Reade are joined by political commentator Jimmy Dore to talk about Trump’s new hair and new term, Ukraine negotiations, Iran, the current state of the US military, the Charlie Kirk assassination, the Epstein files, and much more. Is the US stretched too thin to win two wars at once? Dore argues the Iran conflict drained missile stockpiles meant for Ukraine – so what does that say about America’s real military capacity, and who might be watching closely? Does it actually matter who wins the US midterms? Dore says no, arguing both parties answer to the same donors regardless of outcome. Is voting still a real lever for change? What really shifted Trump between his first and second terms? Dore lays out a theory involving lawsuits, imprisoned allies, and the Epstein files – and on the ground, how much of the anger Tara found in the US is about foreign policy versus the cost of living?
